intro_en:
From the Hula Valley we climb up to the Ramim Ridge, with fine views over the Golan, Mount Hermon and the Hula Valley. We pass through the canyon-like channel of Nahal Kedesh and finish at Metzudat Koach (Koach Fortress).
: The new segment 2 runs from Banias to Tel Hai.
character_en: Most of the route follows dirt roads on an uphill trend; there are shaded sections inside the forest with rest spots. The last part of the route passes through a canyon-like streambed, climbing and descending over rock steps.
shortcuts_en: The route can be shortened and ended at Road 886, before the descent into the Nahal Kedesh channel.
transport_en: At the start and end points – at the entrance to Kfar Giladi and at Yesha Junction, near Metzudat Yesha.
pois_en: Tel Hai Sculpture Garden, Ramim Ridge, Nahal Kedesh, Metzudat Koach.
important_en: Walking in the Nahal Kedesh canyon after rain or when the ground is wet is dangerous. The walk through the Nahal Kedesh canyons looks very short on the map, but it takes at least an hour for a fast hiker and at least two hours for a group.
description_en:
The segment begins at the parking lot of the Roaring Lion monument in Tel Hai. From the parking lot we set out on a path that skirts the Kfar Giladi cemetery from the south. Beside the path is a display of several historical photographs showing the sculpting and creation of the Roaring Lion statue by the sculptor Avraham Melnikov.
We carefully cross the access road to Kfar Giladi and reach a footpath leading to an underpass beneath Road 9977. Coming out of the underpass we pass through the Tel Hai Sculpture Garden, on the way to the entrance to the Naftali Hills Forest. The trail enters among the forest trees and begins a gentle climb up Mount Ramim.
Along the way we pass fine lookouts over the valley, the Golan and Mount Hermon, cross a "geological park", and pass beneath the Manara Cliff cable car.
Toward the end of the route we reach the Nahal Kedesh canyon – a slightly challenging walk in a rocky streambed with rock steps and small dry waterfalls. The walk through Nahal Kedesh runs through two short V-shaped canyons.
It is important to watch the trail marking: take care not to walk past the trail's turn to the right by mistake!
In March the Nazareth iris blooms a little above the stream's northern channel, on the north side, about 300 meters from the start of the descent into the channel.
On the southern side of the canyon the trail leaves the shaded stream and for about 10 minutes passes through open landscape to the entrance to the Metzudat Koach compound – where there is a grove, a memorial and a mass grave of those who fell in the battles to capture the fortress in the War of Independence.
Shortcut options
A blue-marked trail climbing steeply to Kibbutz Manara.
A blue-marked trail climbing to the Yiftah Fissures (Sidkei Yiftah), north of Kibbutz Yiftah.
Exit to the Yesha Junction–Yiftah road before the descent into Nahal Kedesh.
nearby_en: The HaShomer Museum in Kfar Giladi.
The Re'ut (Comradeship) Museum at Metzudat Koach.
author_en: Itzik Ben Dov, trail-marking coordinator, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI).
